# Synthetic MIDI scores (test and gas fixtures)

[`scores.json`](scores.json) holds five synthetic Standard MIDI Files, generated by [`scripts/gen_midi_fixtures.mjs`](../../../scripts/gen_midi_fixtures.mjs) (Node built-ins only, deterministic). They are the scores of the `midi_segment` gas measurements (through the generated [`tests/class_fixtures.cairo`](../../class_fixtures.cairo)) and token 4's score in [`examples/beast_consumer`](../../../examples/beast_consumer). They are test fixtures only: the class never contains them. Like the rest of the repository, they are Apache-2.0.

## Regenerating

From the repository root, regenerate the scores, then the files built from them:

```sh
node scripts/gen_midi_fixtures.mjs                          # tests/fixtures/midi/scores.json
npm run gen:page                                            # tests/class_fixtures.cairo
(cd examples/beast_consumer && node scripts/gen_fixtures.mjs)  # src/beast_data.cairo, tests/golden.cairo
```

`node scripts/gen_midi_fixtures.mjs --check` fails if `scores.json` is out of date, and CI's `generated` job regenerates it and fails on any diff. [`scripts/gen_midi_fixtures.test.mjs`](../../../scripts/gen_midi_fixtures.test.mjs), part of `npm test`, parses every score independently and checks the structure below.

## The scores

Each score is a five-voice round. A seeded subject in a key and scale runs over a four-chord progression of two beats per chord. Every voice plays it in its own octave, entering two bars after the previous voice, so all the voices sound over the same chord; each voice then closes on the tonic.

| Score | Bytes | Tempo (µs per quarter) | Loop | Notes | Key | Progression |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `genesis` | 816 | 455,000 | 25.48 s | 79 | D dorian | i IV i VII |
| `threshold_1` | 1,541 | 500,000 | 38 s | 159 | A minor | i VI III VII |
| `threshold_3` | 2,266 | 500,000 | 46 s | 238 | F major | I vi IV V |
| `veteran` | 2,991 | 500,000 | 54 s | 319 | E harmonic minor | i iv V i |
| `heaviest` | 3,716 | 455,000 | 55.51 s | 401 | G mixolydian | I VII IV I |

They stand in for the production scores of the onchain Beast music composer ([loothero/midi_fun_contract](https://github.com/loothero/midi_fun_contract)), whose size slots give them their names. No data, melody or algorithm comes from it. Each score has exactly the size and tempo of the production score it replaces, so every gas figure, which depends only on the MIDI's length, is unchanged. The structure matches too:

- Standard MIDI File format 1 at 480 ticks per quarter: a tempo track (one tempo meta event, then End-of-Track) and five voice tracks on channels 0-4;
- notes on a quarter-note grid, velocities 92-115 (production: 90 and 110);
- a status byte on every event (no running status), and note-offs as `0x80` with velocity 64;
- End-of-Track at the end of every track, with exact chunk lengths;
- loops of 25-56 s (production: 12.74-63 s).

The generator fits each size exactly: the subject grows while the score fits, then the closing cadences take up the rest, 9 bytes per extra note and 1 byte per quarter rest before a cadence note. All five scores pass the page's MIDI checks (`checkMidi` in [`player/player.js`](../../../player/player.js)).
